admin_is_not_a_reviewer: ADMIN holds no expert_review.* permission. An administrator who must review holds a separate account whose exact role is EXPERT_REVIEWER, and WP-22's assignment check and payload permit still apply to it.
authentication_does_not_grant_curation_a: curation.administer permits operating the curation tooling. It is not authority to author, review or adjudicate a revision: WP-09's separation-of-duty rules govern those and no application role overrides them.

permissions.rationale: Every role may hold an account. Refusing this to a role would make the account unusable rather than restricted.
permissions.title: Authenticate and start a session

permissions.rationale: A user must always be able to end their own session; a logout that could be forbidden is a session that cannot be revoked by the person most likely to notice it was stolen.
permissions.title: End one's own session

permissions.rationale: Bounded to the actor string and the role. There is no personal detail to read, because none is stored.
permissions.title: Read one's own actor identifier and role

permissions.rationale: The representative workflow. Permitted to every role because the input is a synthetic or development case, never a patient.
permissions.title: Run a demo assessment

permissions.rationale: Reading a result the same deployment produced. Holdout payloads are not reachable through this permission; WP-18's access policy governs those separately and refuses regardless of role.
permissions.title: Read an assessment result

permissions.rationale: Public scientific nomenclature. Refusing it would not protect anything and would make the interface unusable.
permissions.title: Read the gene and drug catalogue

permissions.rationale: Traceability is the product. A finding whose citation cannot be opened is an assertion.
permissions.title: Read an evidence record

permissions.rationale: The dashboard publishes counts and empty states, never a holdout case or an expert response.
permissions.title: Read the public validation dashboard

permissions.rationale: Only assignments belonging to the caller. ADMIN is excluded: an administrator who could enumerate assignments could enumerate the expert-holdout set.
permissions.title: List one's own review assignments

permissions.rationale: Holding this permission does not produce an assignment. WP-22 refuses an unassigned case with the same answer it gives for a case that does not exist.
permissions.title: Open an assigned review

permissions.rationale: The blinded half of the protocol. An administrator recording an expectation would be the system predicting its own output.
permissions.title: Record a blinded expected response

permissions.rationale: The one-way door. No role may pass it without an assignment and a locked expectation, and no permission here can substitute for either.
permissions.title: Reveal the system result

permissions.rationale: Records AGREE, PARTIAL or DISAGREE against a revealed result.
permissions.title: Close an assigned review

permissions.rationale: Append-only amendment by the reviewer who made the record.
permissions.title: Append a review correction

permissions.rationale: Release identity is what every audit row and every assessment pins.
permissions.title: Register a release bundle

permissions.rationale: Moves the pointer every subsequent assessment reads.
permissions.title: Activate a release

permissions.rationale: The recovery path. Audited with both sides of the pointer move.
permissions.title: Roll back to a previous release

permissions.rationale: Ends a release's eligibility without deleting its evidence.
permissions.title: Retire a release

permissions.rationale: Which sources may be published from. A scientific decision recorded by an operator, not made by one.
permissions.title: Administer the scientific source policy

permissions.rationale: Operating the tooling. This is NOT authority to author, review or adjudicate a revision: WP-09's separation of duty governs those and is unchanged by any application role.
permissions.title: Operate the curation workflow

permissions.rationale: Validation and deprecation of rules under the approved protocol.
permissions.title: Administer computable rules

permissions.rationale: Freeze, reopen and retire. A frozen ruleset is what a release pins.
permissions.title: Administer ruleset versions

permissions.rationale: Account lifecycle. Never deletion: a deleted user takes the subject of their own audit history with them.
permissions.title: Create, disable, lock and re-role local users

permissions.rationale: Safe projections only. The reader exposes no payload, no expected response and no secret.
permissions.title: Read the governed audit trail

permissions.rationale: Reports the first break and its position, never the content of any event.
permissions.title: Verify the audit hash chain

role_hierarchy_note: null, and not an empty list: there is no hierarchy to describe. Every permission names its holders explicitly, so adding a role adds a column of decisions rather than inheriting a set.
